vocabulary.meaning_en: a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a building
vocabulary.example: They live in a small apartment downtown.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building where people live
vocabulary.example: Their house has a red door.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large, luxurious house, often with a garden
vocabulary.example: They rented a villa by the sea for the summer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small, cozy house, usually in the countryside
vocabulary.example: My grandparents live in a cottage near the lake.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large building where college students live
vocabulary.note_ar: dorm اختصار dormitory (أمريكي)، وفي بريطانيا hall of residence
vocabulary.example: I lived in a dorm in my first year at university.
vocabulary.note_en: "Dorm" is short for "dormitory" (American). In Britain, people say "hall of residence".

vocabulary.meaning_en: a very small apartment with one main room for living, eating and sleeping
vocabulary.example: A studio is cheaper than a two-bedroom flat.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an outdoor platform that sticks out from the wall of a building
vocabulary.example: The landlord was watering plants on the balcony.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an area where flowers, plants or vegetables are grown
vocabulary.example: She grows tomatoes in her garden.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building or room for keeping a car
vocabulary.example: The house comes with a garage.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the top covering of a building
vocabulary.example: Rain came through a hole in the roof.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large door in a fence or outside wall
vocabulary.example: Close the gate so the dog doesn't run out.

vocabulary.meaning_en: money you pay to live in a place; to pay to use a property
vocabulary.example: The rent is due on the first of the month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a legal agreement to rent a property for a fixed time
vocabulary.example: We signed a one-year lease.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the owner of a house or apartment that is rented to others
vocabulary.example: Call the landlord if the heater breaks.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who pays rent to live in a property
vocabulary.example: The new tenants move in next week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: money paid in advance as security when renting
vocabulary.example: You'll get your deposit back when you leave.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a formal written agreement between two or more people
vocabulary.example: Read the contract carefully before you sign it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an amount of money you pay every month
vocabulary.example: The monthly payment includes water and electricity.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long bank loan used to buy a house
vocabulary.example: They took out a mortgage to buy their first home.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the act of selling something
vocabulary.example: That house is for sale.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building or land that someone owns
vocabulary.example: This property belongs to my uncle.
vocabulary.note_en: "Private property" is land or a building that belongs to someone, so others can't go in.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who helps people buy, sell or rent property
vocabulary.note_ar: real estate agent أمريكي، estate agent بريطاني
vocabulary.example: The agent showed us three apartments.
vocabulary.note_en: "Real estate agent" is American; "estate agent" is British.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a piece of metal used to open a lock
vocabulary.example: The landlord gave us the keys.

vocabulary.meaning_en: with furniture already in it
vocabulary.example: We want a furnished flat because we have no furniture.

vocabulary.meaning_en: without furniture
vocabulary.example: Unfurnished apartments are usually cheaper.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a lot of space
vocabulary.example: The living room is bright and spacious.

vocabulary.meaning_en: warm, comfortable and relaxing
vocabulary.example: It's a small but cozy cottage.

vocabulary.meaning_en: of the newest design or technology
vocabulary.example: The kitchen has modern appliances.

vocabulary.meaning_en: of an old style, not modern
vocabulary.example: The house was full of old-fashioned furniture.

vocabulary.meaning_en: covered with rust (the red-brown layer on old metal)
vocabulary.example: The old bike had a rusty chain.
vocabulary.note_en: "Rust" is the red-brown layer that forms on old metal.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to tell someone about a possible danger
vocabulary.note_ar: حرف w في البداية يغيّر صوت ar إلى or: /wɔːrn/
vocabulary.example: He warned us about the ice on the road.
vocabulary.note_en: The "w" at the start changes the "ar" sound to "or": /wɔːrn/.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to show something by holding your finger toward it
vocabulary.example: She pointed to the house on the hill.

vocabulary.meaning_en: thinking about real facts and what is possible
vocabulary.example: Be practical — we can't afford a villa.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give something and receive something in return
vocabulary.example: The friends exchanged nervous looks.
vocabulary.note_en: "Exchange looks" means to look at each other.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to move your head up and down to say yes
vocabulary.example: He nodded and said, "Yes, I agree."

vocabulary.meaning_en: an open area around a house
vocabulary.note_ar: backyard خلف البيت، front yard أمامه
vocabulary.example: The kids are playing in the backyard.
vocabulary.note_en: The "backyard" is behind the house; the "front yard" is in front of it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take money or things from a person or place, often using force
vocabulary.example: Two men robbed the bank yesterday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take something secretly without permission
vocabulary.example: Someone stole my phone on the bus.

fine_lines.title: yard vs garden
fine_lines.explanation_ar: yard هي أي مساحة مفتوحة حول البيت، سواء كان فيها عشب أو بلاط أو تراب (backyard خلف البيت، front yard أمامه). garden مساحة مصممة خصيصاً للزراعة: زهور ونباتات وخضروات. فالأرض المبلّطة أو الترابية بدون زرع تكون yard وليست garden.

examples.sentence: We parked the bikes in the yard.
Their front yard is covered with stones.
My mother grows roses in her garden.
We have a small vegetable garden.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A "yard" is any open area around a house, with grass, stones or soil (the "backyard" is behind the house, the "front yard" in front). A "garden" is an area made for growing things: flowers, plants and vegetables. So an area with only stones or soil and no plants is a yard, not a garden.

fine_lines.title: rob vs steal
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان بمعنى «يسرق». rob غالباً سرقة بالقوة أو التهديد، ويأتي بعدها الشخص أو المكان الذي تمت سرقته. steal سرقة في الخفاء، ويأتي بعدها الشيء المسروق نفسه. باختصار: you rob a person or a place, but you steal an object.

examples.sentence: Someone robbed me in the street.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean to take something that isn't yours. "Rob" usually involves force or threats, and it is followed by the person or place. "Steal" is done secretly, and it is followed by the thing taken. In short: you rob a person or a place, but you steal an object.

fine_lines.title: lease vs contract
fine_lines.explanation_ar: contract أشمل: أي اتفاق رسمي مكتوب (عقد بيع، عقد عمل، عقد إيجار...). lease هو عقد الإيجار فقط.

examples.sentence: She signed a two-year work contract.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A "contract" is more general: any official written agreement (for buying, for work, for renting...). A "lease" is only a contract for renting.

fine_lines.title: landlord vs tenant
fine_lines.explanation_ar: landlord هو مالك العقار الذي يؤجّره للناس. tenant هو المستأجر الذي يدفع الإيجار ليسكن فيه.

examples.sentence: The tenant paid the rent on time.

fine_lines.explanation_en: The "landlord" is the owner who rents a property to people. The "tenant" is the person who pays rent to live there.

expressions.meaning_ar: يجعل الجمهور يصفّق بحرارة أو يضحك بشدة / «يكسّر الدنيا»
expressions.example: Ali's joke brought the house down.
expressions.meaning_en: to make an audience clap or laugh very loudly

expressions.example: There's a flat for rent on the second floor.
expressions.meaning_en: available to rent / available to buy

expressions.example: Don't go in — this is private property.
expressions.meaning_en: land or a building that belongs to someone, so others may not enter

expressions.example: When the teacher said "surprise test", the students exchanged nervous looks.
expressions.meaning_en: to look at each other in a worried way

expressions.example: They took out a mortgage for thirty years.
expressions.meaning_en: to borrow money from a bank to buy a home

expressions.example: You have to pay two months' rent in advance.

grammar.title: Past perfect continuous: clues to a past situation
grammar.explanation_ar: فكّر فيه مثل أدلة مسرح الجريمة: رأيت حالة في الماضي (نصفها بالماضي البسيط)، وسببها نشاط كان مستمراً قبلها مباشرة (نصفه بالماضي التام المستمر had been + ing). had been ثابتة مع كل الضمائر.
examples: Ali was tired because he had been working all day.
The landlord's hands were dirty because he had been watering the plants.
Omar was sweating because he had been running in the park.
grammar.explanation_en: Think of it like clues at a crime scene: you saw a situation in the past (past simple), and its cause was an activity that had been going on just before it (past perfect continuous: had been + -ing). "Had been" stays the same with every subject.

grammar.title: rob + person/place, steal + thing
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد rob نذكر الضحية (شخص أو مكان)، وبعد steal نذكر الشيء المسروق. نقول: He robbed the shop / He stole money from the shop. ولا نقول: He stole the shop.
examples: My bike was stolen last night.
grammar.explanation_en: After "rob", we name the victim (a person or place). After "steal", we name the thing taken. We say: He robbed the shop / He stole money from the shop. We don't say: He stole the shop.

questions.question: The person who owns a flat and rents it to others is the:
questions.explanation_en: The landlord is the owner who rents a property to others.

questions.question: Money you pay in advance as security when you rent a flat is a:
questions.explanation_en: A deposit is money paid in advance as security.

questions.question: A thief ___ my phone while I was sleeping on the train.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد steal يأتي الشيء المسروق، والسرقة كانت خفية.
questions.explanation_en: After "steal" comes the thing taken, and it was done secretly.

questions.question: Two men ___ the bank last night and took all the money.
An area around the house covered only with stones is a:
questions.explanation_ar: yard أي مساحة مفتوحة حول البيت، أما garden فلابد أن تكون مزروعة.
questions.explanation_en: A yard is any open area around a house; a garden must have plants.

questions.question: Ali was tired because he ___ all day.
questions.explanation_ar: سبب مستمر لحالة في الماضي = الماضي التام المستمر.
questions.explanation_en: A continuing cause of a past situation uses the past perfect continuous.

questions.question: "The comedian brought the house down." This means:
choices: The audience laughed and clapped a lot.
questions.explanation_ar: bring the house down = جعل الجمهور يضحك ويصفق بشدة.
questions.explanation_en: "Bring the house down" means to make the audience laugh and clap a lot.

Which is a contract ONLY for renting?
questions.explanation_ar: lease = عقد إيجار فقط، و contract أشمل.
questions.explanation_en: A lease is only a contract for renting; "contract" is more general.
